ai.description: *Rhinophis goweri* is a small, cylindrical shield-tailed snake reaching 20–25 cm. It is uniform dark brown to black with a distinct, blunt, scale-covered tail tip and tiny, vestigial eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhinophis goweri* is uniquely distinguished from other Indian shield-tails by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange lateral stripe along its body.
ai.habitat: *Rhinophis goweri* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats of India, typically inhabiting moist deciduous and evergreen forests at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Rhinophis goweri* is a secretive, burrowing snake that remains primarily subterranean, emerging to the surface mainly during or after heavy monsoon rains.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhinophis goweri* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a small litter of 2–4 offspring. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, peaking between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rhinophis goweri* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, specifically found in the Sivagiri hills at elevations around 1,200 meters.
